summary.oneLiner: Vertically-integrated cotton/blended yarn + fabric exporter delivering record quarterly revenue on demand recovery and yarn-spread expansion (~INR125/kg), with a large ~INR1,100 cr capex (spinning +22k t to ~130k t; fabric +35 mn m to ~75 mn m) commercializing H2 FY27 that should lift top line ~30-35% and shift mix toward higher-margin value-added/finished fabric.

thesis (one line): Vertically-integrated cotton/blended yarn + fabric exporter delivering record quarterly revenue on demand recovery and yarn-spread expansion (~INR125/kg), with a large ~INR1,100 cr capex (spinning +22k t to ~130k t; fabric +35 mn m to ~75 mn m) commercializing H2 FY27 that should lift top line ~30-35% and shift mix toward higher-margin value-added/finished fabric.
scorecard (qoq / yoy):
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | QoQ | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | INR859.8 cr | +7.4% | +2.2% | **Highest-ever quarterly revenue**; driven by demand recovery + higher yarn prices |
| EBITDA | INR130.4 cr | +16.9% | +8.4% | Realization + operational efficiency + cost-saving |
| EBITDA margin | 15.17% | +124 bps (vs 13.93%) | +87 bps (vs 14.30%) | Above FY26 full-year 14.09% |
| PAT (reported) | INR57.4 cr | +29.2% | +23.7% | EPS INR10.20; Cash EPS INR16.74 |
| PAT (normalized) | ~INR57.4 cr | — | — | No one-offs flagged; mgmt margins discussed ex-inventory gains |
| **Cotton-yarn spread** ⭐ | **~INR120-125/kg** (33-34 ct avg) | up from ~INR110 last qtr (+INR10-15) | — | **CALL OUT:** mgmt calls INR125 the "median"; INR90 historical floor (now ~INR100 inflation-adjusted), peak ~INR140-150 post-COVID; sees INR120-125 sustainable |
| Net debt/equity | 0.76x | — | 0.89x (Mar'25) | Deleveraging continues |
| Volume / utilization | Spinning >98%, woven fabric >90% | — | — | Peak-level utilization (call-out below) |

**FY26 full year:** Revenue INR3,213.9 cr (−2.8% YoY, on lower H1 yarn/RM prices); EBITDA INR452.8 cr (−4% YoY); margin 14.09% (vs 14.26%); PAT INR177.6 cr (+1.2%); EPS INR31.58, Cash EPS INR57.93. Exports 61.9% of FY26 revenue (Q4: ~63%). Revenue mix FY26 — yarn 74%, fabric 21%, others 5%. Dividend INR3/share (30%).

**⭐ Capex ramp call-out:** Already >INR300 cr spent of ~INR1,100 cr project (incl ~INR140 cr machinery advances + INR55-60 cr modernization already capitalized; CWIP ~INR100 cr). Balance to be spent in FY27; fabric capacity starts Oct-Dec FY27, spinning Jan-Feb FY27. Plus separate ~INR230-240 cr energy/renewable capex (not originally planned).
guidance (critical):
- **Margin:** Normalized EBITDA margin range **16%-20%** (product profile dependent); expects to fall in that range in **FY27**. (Mgmt declined a hard number but engaged questioners on 17-18% scenario.)
- **Yarn spread:** ~INR120-125/kg viewed as sustainable "median"; floor now ~INR100 (inflation-adjusted from INR90).
- **Volume / utilization:** Spinning ~97-98%, fabric 90%+ to continue for next 2 quarters until new capacity arrives (some summer dip due to heat).
- **Capex ramp:** New capacity commercializes H2 FY27 — fabric (Oct-Dec'26), spinning (Jan-Feb'27); renewable power H2. Asset turn ~1:1 on new capex (1.2-1.3x company-wide ex-renewable).
- **Capacity ramp:** Spinning +22,000 t → ~130,000 t; fabric +35 mn m → ~75 mn m (errata-corrected). End-to-end finished/value-added fabric.
- **Top line:** Capex should add >INR1,000 cr revenue; yarn-price normalization adds ~5-7% of existing turnover; combined mgmt expects to add **~30-35%** to existing revenue going forward.
- **Renewable savings:** ~INR50 cr/annum at full ramp; ~INR30-35 cr in current year (~1% of margin).
- **Peak/total debt:** ~INR1,900-2,000 cr including working capital post-project.
demand: Demand improved in Q4 across both domestic and export — driven by US tariff removal, restocking across downstream channels, and longer transit times prompting earlier buying. H1 FY26 had demand destruction/underutilization from US tariff uncertainty; H2 hit by West Asia conflict (supply-chain disruption, higher freight/transit). Exports ~63% of Q4 revenue. India export of yarn ~100 mn kg/yr industry-wide expected to hold, with ~5-10% incremental demand (helped by China buying more). China share of Nitin's shipments rose 10-11% → 15-16% in March (was 30%+ four years back).
segment (yarn / fabric):
- **Yarn (74% FY26):** Cotton + blended/synthetic. Spread ~INR120-125/kg. Synthetic (pure) margins static; blended (PC/cotton-blended) margins improved. Polyester prices +20%+ post-war; cotton +INR30-35/kg over 3 months (polyester +INR25-27/kg) — no advantage to shift poly→cotton currently. Synthetic blended exports (PV, etc.) to Asia/Middle East/Africa hit by logistics, creating domestic oversupply pressure.
- **Fabric (21-22% FY26):** Woven ~18% (errata; said 20%), knitted ~4% (errata; said 2-3%). Fabric prices move with a lag — March yarn increases now translating into fabric; knit realization +~5% QoQ, woven +~2-2.5% QoQ. **Finished fabric margins structurally superior to yarn margins.** Knitted fabric production was DOWN (heavy US exposure, low-value item hit by 50% tariff); recovering as tariff normalizes — normal 65-70% utilization expected back in ~1-1.5 yrs.
growth / optionality:
- Large integrated capex (spinning +22k t, fabric +35 mn m) commercializing H2 FY27; completely integrated end-to-end finished fabric (value-add).
- Mix shift toward value-added/finished fabric to improve structural margin.
- **FTAs as optionality:** India-UK FTA "to fructify soon" (eliminates duty disadvantage vs competitors); India-EU FTA ~couple quarters out — big boost; European brands already inquiring/planning to diversify sourcing to India (China+1 / geopolitical-stability play). New Zealand FTA + existing Australia presence = geographic expansion.
- Decade track record: revenue/EBITDA/PAT grown ~3-4x; >INR2,000 cr cumulative CFO.
- Future capex: "many things on the drawing board," no number yet.
margins & cost (cotton, power):
- Cotton: international ~$0.63-0.64/lb and domestic INR52,000-55,000/candy were 3-4 yr lows till Dec'25; now trending up but India-international parity holds. Govt removed cotton import duty Aug-Dec'25 (industry pushing for permanent/another removal).
- Gas-based yarn very small; gas cost ~1.7x vs Feb but immaterial and passed on (global phenomenon).
- Power: renewable footprint expanding — Q4 added 10 MW hybrid PPA (INR9.5 cr, operational Q3'27); ~75 MW renewable added in year incl PPAs → near 100 MW total; 50-55% of present+future power from renewables. Savings ~INR50 cr/annum at full ramp.
- Freight: sea freight to Europe +75-80% vs Feb, rest of world +15-20%; mostly passed on (FOB sales); transit +~2 weeks. Already factored in numbers (normalized since March).
capex (large expansion — watch ramp): ~INR1,100 cr core project: spinning +22,000 t (→~130,000 t), fabric +35 mn m (→~75 mn m). >INR300 cr already spent (CWIP ~INR100 cr + ~INR140 cr advances + INR55-60 cr capitalized modernization); balance in FY27. Fabric live Oct-Dec FY27, spinning Jan-Feb FY27. Separate ~INR230-240 cr renewable/energy capex (added, not originally planned). Asset turn ~1:1 on new capex. **Watch H2 FY27 ramp timing.** RIPS incentives apply (capital subsidy 20-25/27% over 10 yrs; interest subsidy 5% term loan or 2.5% eligible FI for 5 yrs; electricity duty / mandi tax / land rebates).
capital allocation (debt): Net D/E down to 0.76x (from 0.89x). Balance financing via internal accruals + debt. Peak/normal total debt ~INR1,900-2,000 cr post-project (incl WC). Avg cost of borrowing ~5.6% (term), WC <7%, blended ~6.5%. Dividend INR3/share (30%).
risks:
- Cotton price: upward trend resuming; India-international parity dependence; lobbying for duty removal — outcome govt-dependent.
- China / export demand: West Asia/Iran-US conflict disrupting transit (esp. Europe) and freight; synthetic export logistics hit. US apparel inflation — a further 5-10% retail price rise could dent demand.
- Capex execution / ramp: H2 FY27 timing; ~INR1,900-2,000 cr peak debt.
- Knitted fabric: lost some US customers during tariff period; rebuild over 1-1.5 yrs.
- FTA timing slippage (EU another couple of quarters; duty removal uncertain).
mgmt tone: Confident and measured. "Highest ever quarterly revenue," constructive on demand recovery, FTAs and spread sustainability; firmly declined hard margin/segment-margin guidance (consistent 16-20% range repeated). Realistic on macro/tariff/inflation ("quite a macro question, very difficult to predict"). Declined inventory disclosure.
non-obvious:
- Spread INR90 floor should now be read as ~INR100 due to inflation in power/labor/component costs — re-rating of "normal" spread.
- China contribution to spread increase deliberately downplayed (10-11%→15-16% shipment share, not 30%+ of old) — mgmt won't attribute margin gain to China alone; restocking + transit-time fear + RM-cost floor are bigger drivers.
- Poly→cotton substitution thesis dismissed (cotton rose more than poly in INR/kg terms; poly still cheaper).
- Knit fabric weakness was tariff-driven (50% US tariff on low-value knits), now reversing.
- Renewable capex (INR230-240 cr) was unplanned add-on within the year.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ Beneficiary of US tariff normalization (10% vs feared 20-50%) and demand restocking.
- ⭐ Structural beneficiary of India-UK & India-EU FTAs (duty-disadvantage elimination, China+1 sourcing diversification to India) — finished-fabric and yarn demand uplift.
- ⭐ Beneficiary of domestic capacity rationalization (obsolete spinning capacity exited) supporting sustainable spreads.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.
